# University of North Texas — Nanoscale Energy Transport Lab

## Why it matters internationally

The Nanoscale Energy Transport Lab in UNT's Department of Mechanical Engineering
develops micro- and nanoscale coatings that control thermal radiation, with
spacecraft thermal regulation as an explicit application. It leads the NASA
M-STAR project ProTECC on electrochromic coatings that combine radiative heat
switching with dust mitigation, and has published broadband reflectance and
room-temperature emittance of lunar dust simulants from 400 nm to 20 µm. Its
strength lies in engineered emitters for space rather than in dedicated emissivity
metrology.

## Scope of activity

- **Quantities:** spectral reflectance (visible to far infrared) · room-temperature thermal emittance · solar absorptivity
- **Spectral range:** 400 nm – 20 µm (lunar dust simulant study)
- **Temperature:** Room temperature
- **Methodology:** Reflectance-based absorptivity and emittance from integrating-sphere and specular spectrometry and FTIR with diffuse and specular accessories, supported by effective-medium modelling; design of micro/nanoscale thermal-radiation coatings for spacecraft thermal control.

**Application domains:** spacecraft thermal-control coatings · lunar exploration: thermal management and dust mitigation (NASA M-STAR ProTECC) · metasurface and thin-film thermal emitters.

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- IR-EMPOWER 2026: Richard Zhang, “Room Temperature Direct Emissivity Measurements of Spacecraft Thermal Materials”; scientific committee
